dhpak2.3:3.2: mātāpitūhi ... ativiya rakkhiyamānā says her parents guarded her on the uppermost floor, not that they provided quarters there.
dhpak2.3:5.2: mātāpitaro nāma ekantahitāva says parents wish one well; the former English called them one's best friends.
dhpak2.3:8.4: na putto na dhītā bhūtapubbā nāma natthi says no one in saṃsāra has not previously been a son or daughter; the former English reversed this.
dhpak2.3:9.5: sakalassa lokassapi me pabbajjāto tava pabbajjā bhaddikā says the grandson's going forth pleases him more than anyone else's.
dhpak2.3:13.1: The fragrant red lotus blooms in the morning without losing its scent; the former English obscured the comparison and omitted its lasting fragrance.
dhpak2.3:16.3: bhattuddesako means distributor of meals, not steward of the Saṅgha.
dhpak2.3:16.5: cūḷapanthako nāma bhikkhu identifies Culla Panthaka as a bhikkhu, not a lay disciple.
dhpak2.3:20.2: saṃkiliṭṭhaṃ ... rajaṃ means soiled with dust; the former English added dye.
dhpak2.3:20.6: rāgarajādayo means the dust of passion and other defilements, not passion and impurity as separate items.
dhpak2.3:21.1: The verse calls passion ‘dust,’ distinguishing it from particles of dirt; the former English reversed the comparison.
dhpak2.3:21.2: vigatarajassa sāsane means the Dispensation of one free from dust, not a Dispensation without stain.
dhpak2.3:22.1: The verse calls hatred ‘dust,’ distinguishing it from particles of dirt; the former English reversed the comparison.
dhpak2.3:22.2: vigatarajassa sāsane means the Dispensation of one free from dust, not a Dispensation without stain.
dhpak2.3:23.1: The verse calls delusion ‘dust,’ distinguishing it from particles of dirt; the former English reversed the comparison.
dhpak2.3:23.2: vigatarajassa sāsane means the Dispensation of one free from dust, not a Dispensation without stain.
dhpak2.3:30.4: anuttaradhammarājatā refers to the Buddha as unsurpassed king of the Dhamma, not a king of ‘ultimate truth.’
dhpak2.3:32.2: ayaṃ parisā ativiya sobhati describes the assembly as exceedingly beautiful, not the Buddha's personal delight.
dhpak2.3:34.3: pādaparikammādīni mentions attending to the teacher's feet and similar duties, not specifically bathing and perfuming them.
dhpak2.3:36.1: kāyakammādīsu refers to bodily deeds and the like; the former English specified thoughts, words, and deeds.
dhpak2.3:40.2: nalāṭante gahetvā places the barber's razor at the king's forehead, not his cheek.
dhpak2.3:46.2: English adds the Cullaseṭṭhi birth story from dead mouse to merchant's succession. Local Pāli only refers to it and quotes the verse; added prose was removed.
dhpak2.3:47.1: pābhatena means a little capital for an undertaking, not an offering or gift. The verse compares it to a small fire blown into flame.
dhpak2.3:50.2: āraddhavīriyo ... mama sāsane says a bhikkhu who arouses energy in the Buddha's dispensation surely masters the transcendent Dhamma.
